hotContext.criticalNews: Robotaxi service expanded to Miami and Dallas on July 3, 2026, with unsupervised vehicles. Production ramping exponentially but software remains primary constraint.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Miami robotaxi launch expands geographic footprint, though fleet size remains modest at ~50 vehicles in Austin per city officials.

positive_signals: Miami service launched with unsupervised vehicles on July 3, 2026
Dallas also added to robotaxi service coverage
negative_signals: Austin fleet still only ~50 vehicles after a year of operation
Software remains limiting factor, not vehicle production
Service expansion limited by FSD capabilities

key_metrics.actual: ~50 vehicles in Austin, new Miami/Dallas launches

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla robotaxi expands to Miami and Dallas on July 3
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 3, 2026, Tesla expanded its unsupervised robotaxi service to Miami and Dallas, marking continued geographic expansion of the Cybercab platform. City officials report Tesla's Austin fleet at approximately 50 vehicles despite a year of operation. Production is ramping exponentially toward year-end per Musk, but software limitations rather than vehicle manufacturing capacity remain the primary constraint on service scaling.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Remote Self-Driving status in the consumer app is real product infrastructure for owner-operated robotaxi fleets, not just a cosmetic UI tweak.

positive_signals: App 4.58.5 shows live 'Self-Driving' indicator when FSD is engaged
Works on HW3 (not only HW4); vehicle software 2026.20.6.1 ~40% fleet rollout
Directly useful for owners whose cars earn robotaxi revenue
negative_signals: Does not expand fleet size or unsupervised city coverage by itself
Still depends on vehicle software rollout reaching the full fleet

key_metrics.target: Remote fleet management for owner-operated robotaxi network
key_metrics.trajectory: Infrastructure for scaled owner fleet; not yet a volume milestone

recentKeyChanges.title: Tesla app adds live Self-Driving indicator for robotaxi owners
recentKeyChanges.description: Tesla app version 4.58.5 (reported July 7, 2026) displays a live blue 'Self-Driving' indicator under the speed readout when FSD is engaged, plus the glowing blue navigation path. Confirmed working on HW3 Model S. Vehicle-side software 2026.20.6.1 has reached ~40% of the fleet. For owners whose vehicles generate robotaxi revenue, this turns the app into a basic fleet monitor — especially relevant as unsupervised service runs in Miami and other cities.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: While geographic expansion to Miami and Dallas signals continued commitment, the underlying reality is concerning: Austin fleet remains stuck at ~50 vehicles after a full year of operation, demonstrating failed scaling. Software limitations—not hardware production—remain the fundamental blocker, making city expansion premature without solving the core constraint.
